proposal.blind_spot: Long-scoreboard stalls dominate (66-80%) with DRAM far from saturated, but the optimizer cannot tell whether stalled loads are served from DRAM, L2, or L1, so it cannot choose between reducing memory traffic and raising memory-level parallelism.

rationale.lts__t_sector_hit_rate.pct: LOW -> loads miss to DRAM; cut miss count via vectorized 128-bit loads, fusing multi-pass reads, register/shared-memory reuse and cache blocking / HIGH -> loads are L2-resident; raise MLP instead (more independent loads per thread, unroll, num_stages, occupancy) and skip locality restructuring
rationale.l1tex__t_sector_hit_rate.pct: LOW -> L1 thrashing on re-read data (softmax, cumprod, median-style kernels); stage tiles explicitly in shared memory or registers and use streaming cache modifiers / HIGH -> re-reads already hit L1; just add ILP/prefetching and avoid pointless shared-memory staging overhead

split.chosen_by: llm_tiebreak:High long-scoreboard stall percentage directly marks a memory-latency-bound warp-issue regime, and using that single condition avoids extra sample-specific cuts and empty quadrants.
